choices.text: The student is right - energy and nutrients both loop forever
Energy is not recycled: only about a tenth passes to the next level, the rest is lost as heat.
Energy is recycled, but only by decomposers
Nutrients flow one way and energy loops

questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: Energy is recycled around the food chain like nutrients are. Reteach point: Energy is not recycled: only about a tenth passes to the next level, the rest is lost as heat.
questions.misconception: Energy is recycled around the food chain like nutrients are.
questions.prompt: A student says energy is recycled around the food chain like nutrients are. What is the best correction?

questions.answer: So little energy reaches each next level - only about a tenth - that after a few links there is not enough energy left to support another consumer.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the tenth-at-each-step loss and the heat that carries the rest away.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why a food chain rarely has more than four or five links.

questions.feedback: Photosynthesis is the sink that removes carbon dioxide; respiration, decomposition and burning are sources that return it.
questions.prompt: In the carbon cycle, which process takes carbon dioxide out of the air?

questions.answer: Nutrients (or carbon) loop: they return to soil and air and are reused. Energy only flows: it enters as sunlight and leaves as heat.
questions.feedback: Credit any looping material (nutrients, carbon, water) against energy as the one-way flow.
questions.prompt: Name one thing that loops in an ecosystem and one thing that only flows, and say the difference in a few words.
